decisions.reason: Accepting placeholders, blurbs, and quotes as text-breakup elements does not change author-name, author-photo identity, source, or placement requirements.
The accepted text-breakup approach does not change the required shape or size of author photos.
The source decision does not alter category display, allowed categories, category sources, styling, or placement.
The accepted use of placeholders, blurbs, and quotes does not affect the prohibition on red in the Dorian Vale article.
The general issue-assembly obligation and Flat Plan reference remain valid unchanged; the newly accepted article text-breakup tactics are already owned by the source Requirement.
The source accepts specific article text-breakup elements but does not modify the polished, modern, brand-aligned visual-style requirement.
Marking locations for additional images does not change the requirement to enhance image quality with AI when necessary.
The accepted layout elements do not change the Civic Lantern website as the source of article content.
The article-layout decision does not alter the deferred print deliverable, resolution, or prepress settings.
The accepted text-breakup approach does not change the digital flipbook PDF deliverable or its scope.
The source decision governs article-level text breakup and does not change the independent obligation to create the magazine layout template.
